components.name: NativeSelect
components.description: The DEFAULT select in Toy Mart BD. A real <select> with appearance:none and our own inlined data-URI chevron. Native is the default on Android for six measurable reasons (spec 6.2): (1) It IS the OS picker - Android draws a full-width dialog or wheel with platform momentum scrolling, fling physics and 48dp rows; a JS listbox on the target mid-range Android scrolls at a measurably lower frame rate because every row is a composited DOM node. (2) Zero JavaScript - a custom select costs ~4-6KB gzipped for positioning, collision detection, focus management and type-ahead plus the option list in the payload; against the 120KB checkout JS budget on 4G, a 64-option district selector x3 cascading levels is the difference between meeting and missing it. (3) TalkBack works with zero ARIA - <select> announces role, value, position-in-set and set size natively; every custom listbox re-implements that with aria-activedescendant and that is where the bugs live. Bangla screen-reader support on Android is already thin. (4) It cannot be mispositioned by the virtual keyboard - focusing an input resizes Android's visual viewport, so a JS menu anchored inside a scrolled bottom sheet gets stale coordinates and opens off-screen; the native picker lives outside the web viewport. (5) Autofill - <select autocomplete="address-level1"> participates in Android autofill and the keyboard suggestion strip; a div[role=listbox] does not. A tap saved on the highest-abandonment screen. (6) No scroll-lock, z-index or portal bugs - checkout filters and address flows put selects inside a bottom-sheet Drawer; a native select has nothing to clip. Checkout uses NativeSelect exclusively: district -> upazila -> area. Visually indistinguishable from Select/Trigger by design, so swapping one for the other is a code change with no visual review. Font size is 16px at BOTH sizes (not 15 at Medium) because a <select> under 16px triggers focus-zoom and, unlike the custom Select, there is no way to intercept it.

properties.name: label
properties.note: FILL x HUG, wraps to 2 lines max, never truncates. Per spec 6.7 the label carries the long Bangla string so the explanatory burden is never on the <select>'s own text. NativeSelect has no showLabel and no required property (spec 6.3 omits both); when a required asterisk is needed, use the Input component's label row pattern and raise it as a spec change - do not add an unbound asterisk layer here.

properties.name: value
properties.note: Characters are bound (identical across variants); VISIBILITY is per-variant and hard-set: visible on Filled, Error and Disabled, hidden on Default, Hover and Focus.

properties.name: placeholder
properties.note: Visibility per-variant and hard-set: visible on Default, Hover, Focus; hidden on Filled, Error, Disabled. In code this is <option value="" disabled selected hidden> and, with required on the select, :invalid colours it color/text/tertiary.

properties.name: showHelper
properties.note: Bind on all variants EXCEPT State=Error, where Helper.visible is hard-set false and the binding is omitted, so a designer cannot produce 'State=Default with an error showing' or 'error plus helper'. Error.visible is never a property - it is per-variant (true only on State=Error). In the DOM both nodes always exist.

properties.name: focusVisible
properties.note: Bind on Default, Hover, Filled and Error. OMIT the binding on State=Focus (_focus hard-set true) and on State=Disabled (hard-set false - spec 0.4: disabled controls are removed from the tab order and get no ring). Error+focus = State=Error with focusVisible true: 1.5px color/feedback/danger border plus a teal color/border/focus ring at 4px offset - two different hues, so 'errored' and 'where am I' are never confused.

components.name: Select
components.description: The CUSTOM listbox Select - the EXCEPTION, not the default. Permitted ONLY when at least one of these is true (spec 5.2): the viewport is >=1024px (desktop), OR options need a thumbnail, a price, a swatch or two lines of text, OR the control is in the admin. In every other case - and specifically the checkout district -> upazila -> area cascade, sort order, and any quantity over 10 - use NativeSelect (spec 6), which is the system default because a custom listbox on a mid-range Android is a worse control in six measurable ways (lower-framerate composited rows, 4-6KB of JS against a 120KB checkout budget, re-implemented TalkBack semantics, visual-viewport mispositioning, no Android autofill, and scroll-lock/z-index/portal bugs inside Drawers). Trigger geometry is identical to Input > Field and to NativeSelect > Field. Open is a variant axis because the menu's exact geometry and every keyboard and screen-reader behaviour is specified in that state. Trigger markup: <button role="combobox" aria-expanded aria-controls aria-haspopup="listbox" aria-labelledby>; menu <ul role="listbox">; options <li role="option" aria-selected aria-disabled>.

properties.name: placeholder
properties.note: Visibility per-variant: visible on Default, Hover, Focus; hidden on Filled, Open, Error, Disabled.

properties.name: value
properties.note: Visibility per-variant: visible on Filled, Open, Error, Disabled; hidden on Default, Hover, Focus.

properties.name: showHelper
properties.note: Bind on all variants EXCEPT State=Error (Helper.visible hard-set false, binding omitted).

properties.name: focusVisible
properties.note: Bind on Default, Hover, Filled, Open and Error. OMIT on State=Focus (hard-set true) and State=Disabled (hard-set false).

properties.name: menuSlot
properties.note: The Menu layer's VISIBILITY is per-variant and hard-set - true only on the two State=Open variants, false everywhere else. It is deliberately NOT a BOOLEAN property: a property-bound visible would need setProperties on every instance and would carry one default across the whole set. Only mainComponent is bound, so a designer can swap in Select/Menu with thumbnails, prices or swatches.

components.name: Select/Option
components.description: One row of the custom Select's listbox: <li role="option" aria-selected aria-disabled>. Built BEFORE Select and Select/Menu. 44 FIXED tall (56 when showDescription is true - see notes, the lead sets that per instance because a BOOLEAN property cannot change frame height). A disabled option is NEVER hidden; it shows the reason in description (e.g. 'Out of stock in this size'). Hiding unavailable options is how a shop looks like it has nothing. No _focus layer: DOM focus stays on the trigger and the active option is tracked with aria-activedescendant, so State=Hover doubles as the active-option appearance.

properties.name: label
properties.note: FILL x HUG, wraps to 2 lines in Bangla, Truncate off. The label's text STYLE is per-variant, not a property: Latin/Mobile/body on Default/Hover/Disabled and Latin/Mobile/body-strong (15/600) on Selected.

properties.name: description
properties.default: Out of stock in this size
properties.note: One default across the set, so the string is the disabled-reason wording from spec 5.5; it is invisible by default. Override per instance for non-disabled rows.

properties.name: showDescription
properties.note: A BOOLEAN cannot change the frame height, so when it is turned on the lead must ALSO set that instance's vertical sizing to HUG with min-height 56 and padding Y space/2. See the geometry note on measured height.

properties.name: leadingSlot
properties.note: 24x24 (size/icon-lg) - icon, swatch or thumbnail. Default is the Phosphor icon/circle glyph per spec 0.9 (never a blank frame, which hides layout bugs). Lucide circle maps to Phosphor icon/circle.

components.name: Select/Menu
components.description: The custom Select's popover listbox (<ul role="listbox">). Standalone component so it can be the default of Select's menuSlot INSTANCE_SWAP. Geometry per spec 5.5: surface-raised, 1px border/default, radius/lg, Elevation/Light/e3, space/2 padding, 0 gap between options, min-width = trigger width, max-width 420, max-height 320 then vertical scroll with overscroll-behavior: contain. Rendered in a portal at the document root above the sticky AddToCartBar; inside a Drawer it is portalled into the drawer so the scroll lock does not clip it. Offset space/1 (4) below the trigger, flipping above on collision with a 16px viewport inset.

newTextStyles.name: Latin/Mobile/field-label
newTextStyles.reason: Spec 3.3 / 5.3 / 6.3 require the field label at 'body-sm 14/600'. Latin/Mobile/body-sm matches the 14px size but is weight 400; Latin/Mobile/label matches the 600 weight but is 13px. Neither existing style matches, so this one is new. It is the label style for Input, Textarea, Select and NativeSelect.

newTextStyles.name: Bangla/Mobile/field-label
newTextStyles.reason: Bangla parallel of the above. Line-height is the Latin 1.50 x 1.15 = 1.73 per foundations 5.2; Bangla tracking is 0, absolutely. Figma layers bind to the Latin style; .lang-bn swaps family and line-height at runtime.

newTextStyles.name: Latin/Mobile/body-strong
newTextStyles.reason: Spec 5.5 requires the SELECTED option label at 'color/text/primary (weight 600)' at the body size. Latin/Mobile/body is 15/400 and Latin/Mobile/button is 15/600 but at line-height 120% with 0.002em tracking, which is too tight for an option label that must wrap to 2 lines in Bangla. 15/600 at 160% is new.

notes: KEYBOARD AND SCREEN-READER MODEL (Select, custom). Trigger: <button role="combobox" aria-expanded aria-controls="<menu-id>" aria-haspopup="listbox" aria-labelledby="<label-id>">. Menu: <ul role="listbox" id="<menu-id>">; options <li role="option" aria-selected aria-disabled>. OPEN: Space, Enter, ArrowDown or ArrowUp. WITHIN THE MENU: ArrowDown / ArrowUp move the active option, Home / End jump to first / last, Enter commits, Esc closes and returns focus to the trigger, Tab closes AND commits. TYPE-AHEAD: printable characters jump to the first option starting with the typed buffer; the buffer clears after 800ms. Bangla type-ahead matches on the Bangla label; Banglish matching is a search-field concern, not a Select concern. The active option is tracked with aria-activedescendant and DOM focus STAYS on the trigger (or on the in-menu search field when one is present) - this is why Select/Option has no _focus layer and why State=Hover is also the active-option appearance. Focus is NOT trapped: this is a listbox, not a dialog. Clicking outside commits nothing and closes. The menu is rendered in a portal at the document root with z-index above the sticky AddToCartBar; inside a Drawer it is portalled into the drawer so the scroll lock does not clip it. NativeSelect has no keyboard model of ours at all: the open state is the operating system's, which is the entire point of the component, and <select> announces role, value, position-in-set and set size to TalkBack with zero ARIA.

CASCADE ANNOUNCEMENT (NativeSelect, checkout). <select> takes aria-describedby, aria-invalid and required exactly as <input> does (spec 3.6 markup applies verbatim: error id FIRST in aria-describedby, the error node ALWAYS in the DOM and empty when valid, role="alert" plus an explicit aria-live="polite" to downgrade it, aria-invalid set only while an error shows and REMOVED when valid). Cascade addition: when district changes, upazila and area are reset, their errors cleared, and the reset announced ONCE in a single aria-live="polite" message ('Upazila and area reset - choose again'), not as three separate announcements.

TOKEN NAME DEVIATION: the spec writes spacing/N; the real Figma variables are space/N. Mapping used throughout this manifest: spacing/1 -> space/1 (4), spacing/2 -> space/2 (8), spacing/3 -> space/3 (12), spacing/4 -> space/4 (16). Field heights bind to size/control-md (44) and size/control-lg (52); the 20px chevron binds to size/icon-md; the 24px option leading slot binds to size/icon-lg; 1px borders bind to border-width/hairline and 2px to border-width/strong.

RADIUS VALUE DEVIATION: the spec annotates radius/md as 10, radius/lg as 14 and radius/sm as 6. The real tokens are radius/md=12, radius/lg=16, radius/sm=8. Use the TOKEN NAMES as given here - the field is radius/md (12), the menu radius/lg (16), the option radius/sm (8). The _focus ring radius follows spec 0.2 (host radius + 4 = 16), which is exactly radius/lg, so the ring binds to radius/lg rather than carrying a raw number.

ICON DEVIATIONS (Phosphor replaced Lucide): chevron-down -> icon/caret-down; the error row's alert-triangle -> icon/warning-circle; icon/check is unchanged; the INSTANCE_SWAP default Lucide circle -> icon/circle; the in-menu search prefix uses icon/magnifying-glass. THERE IS NO caret-up IN THE LIBRARY. Spec 5.4's reduced-motion instruction ('swap to icon/chevron-up instantly') is therefore executed as: keep icon/caret-down and apply the 180 degree rotation INSTANTLY with no transition. Phosphor icons are FILLED - every icon layer here is coloured with a FILL and never a stroke.

1.5px ERROR BORDER has no token (border-width/ has only hairline=1 and strong=2). It is a raw 1.5 on the Error variants, which is intentional per spec 0.6 (border widths are not tokenised). Stroke align is INSIDE on every state so the 1 -> 2 -> 1.5 changes never shift the field's outer box or its neighbours; an outside or centred stroke makes the whole form jump 0.5px on focus. The _focus ring is the one exception: CENTER align, inset -4 on all sides, so it sits 4px outside the component bounds.

CHEVRON / PADDING RECONCILIATION - read before building Field. Spec 6.5 says 'padding X space/3 / space/4 with padding-right extended to accommodate the chevron (space/4 + 20 + space/2 = 44 at Large)' AND 'layer order Value (FILL) -> Chevron'. Taken literally that double-counts: the extended padding-right exists in CSS only because the chevron there is a background-image, not a flow item. In Figma the chevron IS a flow child, so Field padding is SYMMETRIC - space/3 (12) at Medium, space/4 (16) at Large - with gap space/2 (8) before a 20px chevron. The value's right edge therefore sits 12+8+20 = 40 from the right at Medium and 16+8+20 = 44 at Large, which reproduces the CSS padding-inline-end exactly. Do NOT also set a 40/44 padding-right.

COMPUTED GEOMETRY (both selects). Authoring width 342 (a 390px BD phone minus space/6 gutters); the root is FILL so the width is nominal. Rows: Label 21 (Latin/Mobile/field-label 14 x 150%) -> gap space/2 (8) -> Field 44 or 52 FIXED -> gap space/1 (4) -> Message 17 (Latin/Mobile/caption 12 x 140% = 16.8). Root HUG height = 94 at Medium, 102 at Large with a helper line; 73 / 81 with showHelper false. Root structure is spec 3.5's two-gap fix: Select (column, gap space/2, HUG x FILL) > [ Label, FieldGroup (column, gap space/1, HUG x FILL) > [ Field, Message ] ] (+ Menu, absolute, for Select only). Clip content MUST be false on the root, on FieldGroup and on Field, or the -4 inset _focus ring is cut off.

MENU GEOMETRY AND MAX-HEIGHT. Select/Menu: VERTICAL, HUG height x FILL width, align top-left, fill color/bg/surface-raised, 1px color/border/default INSIDE, radius/lg, Elevation/Light/e3, padding space/2 (8) all sides, gap space/2 (8) between SearchField and OptionList, and gap 0 INSIDE OptionList. Min-width = the trigger width; max-width 420; MAX-HEIGHT 320, after which set the frame height FIXED 320, turn Clip content ON and scroll vertically with overscroll-behavior: contain. As authored it holds 6 options: 8 + (6 x 44) + 8 = 280, under the 320 cap. 7 options (8+308+8=324) is the first count that exceeds it. In Select, the Menu layer is an instance of Select/Menu with Ignore auto-layout ON, constraints Left+Right / Top, absolute inset left 0 / right 0 and top = Label(21) + 8 + FieldHeight + 4, i.e. top 77 at Medium and top 85 at Large. That is spec 5.5's space/1 (4) offset below the trigger, and it is absolute precisely so an open menu does not push the rest of the form down. At runtime the menu flips above the trigger on collision with a 16px viewport inset.

IN-MENU SEARCH FIELD - internal spec conflict resolved. Spec 5.5 says 'Input Size=Medium pinned at the top, shown when option count > 12'; spec 5.9 overrides it with a reason: 'the in-menu search field uses Input Size=Large (16px) even inside a Medium Select, for the iOS/Android zoom reason in 3.3'. The reasoned override wins: the SearchField layer is an Input instance at Size=Large, showLabel false, showHelper false, prefix true with icon/magnifying-glass, visible FALSE as authored. Turn it on only when the option count exceeds 12. When it is visible, DOM focus sits on it rather than on the trigger, and aria-activedescendant still tracks the active option.

OPTION HEIGHT WITH A DESCRIPTION - measured deviation. Spec 5.5 states 56 when showDescription is true, via 'padding Y space/2 with HUG'. Measured with the real styles that is 8 + 24 (Latin/Mobile/body 15 x 160%) + 21 (Latin/Mobile/body-sm 14 x 150%) + 8 = 61, not 56. Build the set at FIXED 44 with padding Y 0 and, on description instances, set vertical sizing HUG with MIN-HEIGHT 56 and padding Y space/2 - the hug will land at 61 in Latin. Spec 5.9's Bangla worst case (2 label lines + 1 description line) is quoted as 76; with the Bangla parallel styles it measures 8 + 2x27.6 + 24.2 + 8 = 95.4. Menu max-height stays 320 either way: more Bangla lines simply means fewer options visible, which is correct.

VARIANT MATRIX REASONING. NativeSelect 6 States x 2 Sizes = 12. Select 7 States x 2 Sizes = 14; Select/Option 4 States = 4. Per spec 0.3 hover, pressed, focus-visible and disabled are interaction-only and NOT axes - but Input (3.1) is the stated exception and Select / NativeSelect inherit it: a form mockup must show a filled field beside an errored field beside a focused field in one static frame, and Filled and Error are content states a designer cannot reach by hovering. Hover and Focus are on the axis because developers need an exact border spec for each and because error-plus-focus is the one pair that must stay visually distinguishable side by side. Open is on Select's axis because the menu's exact geometry and every keyboard and screen-reader behaviour is specified in that state (spec 5.1). NativeSelect has NO Open state: the open state is the operating system's and it is not ours to design - that is the point of the component.

PROPERTY vs PER-VARIANT DISCIPLINE (binding decision 2). A Figma component property has ONE default across a whole set and it overrides per-variant content, so anything that differs per variant is hard-set on the variant and NOT bound. Bound (identical across variants): all TEXT characters, menuSlot and leadingSlot mainComponent. Hard-set per variant: Value / Placeholder visibility, Error row visibility, Menu visibility, chevron rotation, every fill / stroke / stroke-weight token, and the Selected option's label text style. Partially bound: showHelper (omitted on State=Error) and focusVisible (omitted on State=Focus and State=Disabled). A property-bound visible also requires setProperties on each instance (binding decision 3), which is a second reason Menu visibility is not a boolean.

NO _scrim AND NO _hit44 ON EITHER SELECT. Spec 0.2's _scrim is for controls whose hover is a darkening; both selects express hover as a border swap to color/border/strong (spec 3.4), so no _scrim layer is built - adding one would double the hover signal. No _hit44 either: every target already clears 44 (trigger 44 or 52 x FILL; option 44 x full menu width; the native picker's own rows are 48dp, set by the platform). The chevron, the check icon and the leading slot are decorative and live INSIDE their parent's single tap target, never as separate targets. An interactive in-menu clear control, where present, is IconButton Size=Medium. Adjacent selects in a cascade are separated by at least space/2 (8) so one 44px hit area never overlaps its neighbour's. No _aria-label layer: both selects are labelled by a real <label for>, not aria-label.

DISABLED, ONE RULE (spec 0.4). fill color/bg/subtle, text color/text/tertiary, 1px color/border/default, icon color/text/tertiary, no scrim, no shadow, no focus ring. The helper line also drops to color/text/tertiary. Disabled controls are exempt from WCAG 2.2 contrast minimums; the adjacent explanatory text is not and stays color/text/secondary or stronger. A disabled OPTION is the opposite case - it is never hidden and it states the reason in its description, because hiding unavailable options is how a shop looks like it has nothing.

16px FONT-SIZE RULE. NativeSelect binds Latin/Desktop/body (16px) to Value and Placeholder at BOTH sizes - not Latin/Mobile/body (15) at Medium - because a <select> under 16px triggers the same focus-zoom as an <input> and, unlike the custom Select, there is no way to intercept it (spec 6.4). The custom Select keeps Latin/Mobile/body (15) at Medium and Latin/Desktop/body (16) at Large, matching Input. Independently, every STOREFRONT field - checkout, OTP, address, coupon, search - uses Size=Large; Size=Medium is permitted only in the admin.

TEXT STYLE MAPPING. Spec en/body 15/1.6/400 -> Latin/Mobile/body (exact size match). en/body 16/1.6/400 -> Latin/Desktop/body (exact). en/caption 12 -> Latin/Mobile/caption (exact, 12/500/140%/0.005em). Option description -> Latin/Mobile/body-sm (14/400/150%). Two styles had no size match and are new: Latin/Mobile/field-label (14/600) and Latin/Mobile/body-strong (15/600) - see newTextStyles. Every text layer in this manifest binds to a Latin/* style; the .lang-bn class swaps family and line-height at runtime, never one global line-height.

BANGLA, 40% RULE (spec 0.7, 5.9, 6.7). Bangla option labels run 15-25% longer than English. SELECT TRIGGER: strategy GROW then WRAP. ValueSlot/Value is FILL, single line, Truncate OFF; if a district name plus its Bangla qualifier exceeds the trigger width, change the Field's vertical sizing from FIXED to HUG with MIN-HEIGHT 44 / 52 and let the value wrap to 2 lines. Documentation instance: 'Select / bn wrap'. SELECT/OPTION: label wraps to 2 lines; height goes from FIXED 44 to HUG with min-height 44 and padding Y space/2. NATIVESELECT: strategy GROW then WRAP, with the wrap on the LABEL, not the field - a native <select> truncates with an ellipsis and that is the one truncation this document cannot forbid, because it is the user agent's. All three mitigations are required: (1) BD administrative names are short in Bangla and the measured worst case, 'Chattogram Mohanagar' at 16 characters, fits a 390px select at 16px Anek Bangla with 44px of right padding; (2) the Label is FILL x HUG and wraps to 2 lines so the explanatory burden is never on the select's own text; (3) for the AREA-level select only, echo the selected value below the field as a Helper line, so a truncated value is always readable in full somewhere. Truncation is otherwise FORBIDDEN on every layer here. Height headroom (spec 0.7): a 44 field holds a 27.6px Bangla body line-box with 16.4 to spare; a 52 field has 27.2 - no fixed-height control fails on Bangla. Option text inside the native picker wraps automatically on Android and is not our concern. Build a Bangla documentation instance of each set beside the Latin one.

NUMERALS ARE WESTERN (0-9) IN BOTH LOCALES. This governs every option label, the delivery-charge helper copy and any district code - do not substitute Bengali digits even in the Bangla documentation instances.

MOTION (spec 0.5). Chevron rotation on Open: 180 degrees over base 200ms with standard cubic-bezier(.2,0,0,1). Menu entry uses the same base / standard pair. spring cubic-bezier(.34,1.56,.64,1) is FORBIDDEN here - it is reserved for the Tier 2 add-to-cart confirmation. Everything is wrapped in prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference; the reduced-motion fallback is an instant 180 degree rotation and an instant menu appearance, no transition.
ELEVATION: Elevation/Light/e3 on Select/Menu. The dark build swaps to Elevation/Dark/e3 - the menu is the only elevated surface in either select; triggers never carry a shadow, including on Open.

BUILD ORDER for the lead, since Figma mutations are sequential: (1) create the four new text styles; (2) Select/Option (4 variants) - nothing depends on it yet; (3) Select/Menu, which instances Select/Option and Input; (4) NativeSelect (12 variants); (5) Select (14 variants), whose menuSlot default needs Select/Menu to exist. Select/Menu also instances the existing Input set, so Input must already be built. bindTo.layer values are slash-separated PATHS from the component root, because 'Text' appears once inside Helper and once inside Error.
